# NVIDIA Image Scaling

Vendored from NVIDIA Image Scaling SDK **1.0.3**, commit
`35e13ba316c98eeecf16f37eae70ce88019911f6` of
[NVIDIAGameWorks/NVIDIAImageScaling](https://github.com/NVIDIAGameWorks/NVIDIAImageScaling).
`NIS_Config.h`, `NIS_Main.hlsl`, and `NIS_Scaler.h` are unmodified upstream files.
The MIT license is retained here and in `common/licenses/NVIDIA-NIS-LICENSE.txt`.

`common/tools/embed_nis.py` compiles the HLSL into the checked-in
`common/src/ipod/platform/sdl3/nis_shader.inc`. Regenerate on Windows with:

```powershell
uv run --python 3.12 python common/tools/embed_nis.py
uv run --python 3.12 python common/tools/embed_nis.py --check
```

The script finds the latest installed Windows SDK x64 FXC, or accepts `--fxc PATH`.
This artifact was generated with Windows SDK **10.0.28000.0**. Shader Model 5.0,
32×24 output blocks, 128 threads, viewport bounds, and output clamping are used.
Game builds do not invoke FXC; shader compilation never occurs during gameplay.
The generated bytecode retains NVIDIA's license through the accompanying notice.

The shared D3D11 adapter processes display-referred RGB in bounded 1×–2× passes,
with 35% sharpness only on the final pass and minimum sharpness on preceding
passes. It bypasses enhancement at native size and uses the existing averaging
path for reductions. This is spatial NIS, not DLSS or Tensor-core inference.
